headline: QA-focused signals: GitHub adds coverage ruleset API; agentic QA moves into production (WSO2, DoorDash, Junie); OpenCodeReview and related research worth studying.

top_signal.title: GitHub adds REST API to manage 'Restrict code coverage' ruleset
top_signal.summary: GitHub published a changelog entry announcing a generally available REST API to create, read, and update the 'Restrict code coverage' repository ruleset, enabling programmatic enforcement of minimum or patch coverage thresholds across repos.
top_signal.why_it_matters: QA teams can now automate code-coverage gates at scale and embed coverage policy in infrastructure-as-code and onboarding automation.

items.title: WSO2 Agent Manager reaches GA for enterprise agent governance
items.summary: WSO2 announced general availability of Agent Manager, an open control plane that provides identity, governance, observability, and operational controls for AI agents running across frameworks and runtimes.
items.why_it_matters: Teams deploying test-design or test-execution agents gain a single governance plane to enforce identity, audit, and operational invariants for agentic QA workflows at scale.

items.title: DoorDash published a production multi-agent LLM system for feature-flag cleanup
items.summary: DoorDash described a two-phase agentic pipeline (analysis + parallel cleanup agents) that produces merge-ready PRs for stale feature flags; the system validates builds, tests, patch coverage, and static analysis before opening PRs.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete production example of agents executing code changes with CI-level validation and human checkpoints — a template QA teams can adapt for safe, automated remediation workflows.

items.title: Alibaba open-sources OpenCodeReview — an agentic, deterministic-first code-review CLI
items.summary: OpenCodeReview is a Go-based CLI that combines deterministic pipelines (file selection, rule matching) with an LLM agent for dynamic analysis; it ships benchmarks and prioritizes precision via deterministic components.
items.why_it_matters: QA and engineering-review pipelines can adopt a hybrid deterministic/agent approach to improve review precision while keeping AI-driven analysis auditable and reproducible.

items.title: JetBrains adds /demo to Junie CLI to record agent-driven UI demos and smoke tests
items.summary: Junie’s /demo mode builds and launches apps in Docker, drives the UI via a model with Computer Use capability, records video/screenshots, and generates an HTML report for reviewer inspection and CI integration.
items.why_it_matters: Provides structured, reviewable evidence from agent-driven UI runs; useful for release smoke tests, reviewer sign-off, and making agent results auditable in PRs and CI artifacts.

watch.title: Junie Local: on-device coding agent for Mac (high-resource) — watch adoption
watch.summary: JetBrains published Junie Local (on-device agent) that runs a tuned Qwen3.6-27B model on Apple M5 Macs (≈64 GB RAM), enabling local agent runs with no cloud tokens or telemetry.
watch.why_it_matters: On-device agents remove data-exfiltration concerns and change cost calculus for long-running QA tasks (large refactors, coverage work); watch hardware and scale requirements for team adoption.

learning.title: OpenCodeReview paper — 'Determinism over Non-Determinism for Agent-Based Code Review' (arXiv)
learning.summary: An arXiv preprint accompanying OpenCodeReview explains the deterministic-first architecture for agentic code review and presents benchmarks and trade-offs between precision and recall for agent-driven reviews.
learning.why_it_matters: Studying this paper helps QA leads design hybrid deterministic/agent pipelines, understand evaluation metrics, and plan guardrails to reduce false positives and drift in agent reviews.
